subject: Re: Prepaid commitment — safety net & credit recapture mechanics
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marta López <marta.lopez@evergreen-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Prepaid commitment proposal — first pass on safety net + recapture

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our call, attaching a single-sheet schedule that shows how the annual prepaid wallet would draw down across expected ramp months and two safety mechanisms we discussed: a temporary replenishment (swingline) and a credit recapture clamp for prolonged underuse.

High-level summary (see attached sheet for numbers):
- Commitment: $600k annual prepaid, billed up front for the 12-month term.
- Discount bands: 15% at $600k/yr, 18% at $1M/yr (we can show an uplift schedule if you stretch beyond year 1).
- Ramp: first 3 months expected to consume ~40% of monthly peak; we model gradual ramp, not front-loaded.
- Safety net: a one-time swingline replenishment equal to 10% of the annual wallet that can be pushed once in the term if you exceed burn forecast (subject to finance approval).
- Credit recapture: if trailing 60-day utilization falls below 25% of committed monthly baseline for two consecutive 30-day windows, we propose a partial recapture of up to 20% of remaining prepaid credits, credited back to Redwood and resulting in a pro-rated refund or reduction to next invoice.

Operational notes:
- We provide daily burn reports and a weekly cadence for usage forecasting so you can trigger a replenishment or request a pause.
- Rollover: we can allow a limited rollover of up to 8% of unused credits into the following term for multi-year deals (requires contractual language in MSA).
- Invoice timing: 100% upfront for the annual prepay in the hosted option; Dedicated/Private pricing has different billing cadence.

Next steps: Laura and Ben are looped for finance/legal sizing — if you can confirm what cushion (swingline %) Evergreen would need and whether the recapture clause is acceptable, we can produce a redline-ready schedule and updated MSA language by Thursday.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Evergreen-Prepay-Schedule-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marta López <marta.lopez@evergreen-analytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@evergreen-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Prepaid commitment proposal — safety net & recapture

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. A few quick questions from procurement and our finance lead: 

1) Can you clarify how the 60-day trailing utilization is calculated? Is it rolling daily or fixed calendar windows? We need deterministic language for our auditors.
2) For the swingline (10% replenishment), is that an advance on future credits (i.e., reduces next year's credits if used) or a refundable short-term top-up?
3) You mention an 8% rollover for multi-year deals — can that be increased if we move to a 2-year committed contract?

Also, we're sensitive to an automatic recapture that happens without an opportunity to remediate. Can we add a customer cure period (30 days) and a one-time courtesy extension per year before recapture?

If you can get us redlines for MSA language that map to those three points, procurement will review them next week.

Best,
Marta López
Head of Platform Partnerships | Evergreen Analytics
marta.lopez@evergreen-analytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marta López <marta.lopez@evergreen-analytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prepaid commitment proposal — safety net & recapture

Marta — looping finance & legal on the specific asks. Quick answers and proposed concessions so we can move to a redline: 

1) Utilization window: we can define "60-day trailing utilization" as a rolling daily average over the preceding 60 days (daily usage aggregated and averaged), and include the exact formula in the SOW appendix (we'll provide sample calc in the spreadsheet). That should satisfy audit determinism.

2) Swingline mechanics: it will be treated as an interest-free short-term top-up that draws from the same prepaid wallet; if used, it reduces the remaining wallet balance and is reflected in the monthly reconciliation. It is not a refundable cash advance. We can add a clause that treats it as an "emergency top-up" usable once per 12-month term.

3) Rollover: we can increase rollover to 12% for a 2-year committed deal, and up to 15% if Evergreen moves to a 3-year locked commitment, provided minimum annual spend thresholds are met.

4) Recapture process: agree to a 30-day cure period plus a one-time courtesy 14-day extension per 12-month term before we execute recapture. Execution will require a written notice and an opportunity for Evergreen to request a remediation plan.

Operational asks from our side: 
- We will need an agreed point-of-contact for weekly forecast calls (format: 15-min pulse + updated sheet).
- Please confirm desired tax/billing entity for the upfront invoice.

I'll produce an updated schedule and mark up the MSA with these items today and send as Draft-MSA-redlines.pdf for legal review. Priyom — can you confirm whether finance is comfortable with the swingline being non-refundable and how we should record it in CRM?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marta López <marta.lopez@evergreen-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prepaid commitment proposal — safety net & recapture

Hi Marta / team —

Finance has reviewed and we're aligned with Ben's approach. A few final operational clarifications to include in the redline: 

- Reporting & reconciliation cadence: daily usage file + weekly summary email; monthly invoice reconciliation with a 14-day dispute window.
- Accounting treatment: the swingline will be recorded against the prepaid wallet (reduces remaining prepaid credits) and not treated as a separate receivable; for Evergreen's finance team, we'll provide the ledger export for each monthly reconciliation.
- Credit recapture mechanics: when triggered, Redwood will propose a pro-rated reconciliation amount and either (a) issue a refund to Evergreen's payment method within 30 days or (b) apply a credit to future invoices (customer's choice). This will be spelled out in MSA schedules.

Ben / Jonas — I attached the two artifacts for legal & procurement: Draft-MSA-redlines.pdf and the updated schedule spreadsheet. Marta — once you confirm the cure period and swingline usage policy, we will convert to a DocuSign package and circulate the HubSpot deal link (included in the thread metadata).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

—
Priyom Das
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Draft-MSA-redlines.pdf (redline), Evergreen-Prepay-Schedule-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)
